subject.title: [Tooling]: Add pre/post-update compatibility scanner with risk report and smoke recommendations

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class `doctor --upgrade-scan` or update-integrated upgrade assessment contract, and what are its JSON schema, redaction rules, smoke-check boundaries, and rollback-hint semantics?
rationale: The missing work is a public tooling and report contract with security, session-state, and operator-action implications, not a narrow broken-code repair that automation can safely choose alone.

options.title: Design Core Upgrade Assessment
options.body: Define a core-owned scanner/report contract that composes existing doctor, update, plugin, health, backup, and rollback surfaces without duplicating validators.

options.title: Keep Adjacent Pieces Only
options.body: Treat doctor lint, post-upgrade plugin probes, update dry-run, and docs as sufficient for now while accepting that unified risk scoring and rollback guidance remain absent.

options.title: Defer To External Automation
options.body: Leave the scanner as an external script, plugin, or skill, which avoids a core API commitment but cannot cover missing core upgrade/report contracts.

recommendation.title: Design Core Upgrade Assessment
recommendation.body: Define a core-owned scanner/report contract that composes existing doctor, update, plugin, health, backup, and rollback surfaces without duplicating validators.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current evidence across prior review, current doctor/update history, and the closest merged post-upgrade work.
